Title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
Authors: Jason Wei, Xuezhi Wang, Dale Schuurmans, Maarten Bosma, Brian Ichter,
         Fei Xia, Ed Chi, Quoc Le, Denny Zhou (Google Research, Google Brain)
Year: 2022
Venue: NeurIPS 2022
Citations: 8,432

Abstract:
We explore how generating a chain of thought—a series of intermediate reasoning
steps—significantly improves the ability of large language models to perform
complex reasoning. In particular, we show how such reasoning abilities emerge
naturally in sufficiently large language models via a simple method called
chain-of-thought prompting, where a few chain-of-thought demonstrations are
provided as exemplars in prompting.

Key Findings:
- Chain-of-thought prompting substantially improves performance on arithmetic,
  commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks across multiple LLM families
- The ability emerges as a property of model scale (~100B parameters)
- Works with few-shot prompting; does not require fine-tuning
- Outperforms standard few-shot prompting by large margins on GSM8K (+15.1%)

Methodology:
Few-shot prompting with step-by-step reasoning demonstrations as exemplars.
The model is given a few (question, chain-of-thought, answer) triples as
in-context demonstrations, then asked to produce a chain of thought for a
new question before giving the final answer.
Evaluated on GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, AQuA (arithmetic),
CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA (commonsense), and letter/coin-flip tasks (symbolic).
